Source, state, write authorization and retention boundaries.

reviews.lens: Boutique recruiter operational fit: GET-5-product-v1, baseline d363ac04 plus the manifest-frozen implementation. Synthetic independent recruiter juggling several searches on an iPhone, continuing a note through review, deliberate contact saving, restart and a fork. The intended success is one recoverable contact result and usable continuing context with the original source still inspectable. Actual search load, deadline pressure and field behavior are unavailable.

findings.criterion: Write safety: tell the recruiter whether the prior save is known to have failed
findings.observation: Direct observation: the response-loss screen simultaneously says that the previous outcome is unknown and that the contact was not saved. The frozen fallback error also makes the definite failure claim after an arbitrary save error. The native recovery subsequently finds the committed person and obtains the original-operation receipt. This is contradictory outcome communication, not evidence that the retry creates duplicate contacts.
findings.evidence: /tmp/get5-product-review-v1/evidence/screenshots/07-contact-response-lost-r6.png, pending-write banner and red contact-save error; /tmp/get5-product-review-v1/evidence/screenshots/08-contact-same-operation-restored-r6.png, Contact created receipt; /tmp/get5-product-review-v1/source/apps/ios/Sources/Features/RelationshipAskView.swift:5049-5053 and :5670-5694; /tmp/get5-product-review-v1/source/apps/ios/UITests/CandidateSignalUITests.swift:5031-5068; /tmp/get5-product-review-v1/evidence/get5-ios-ui-final-r6.log:552 records this response-loss/relaunch scenario passing.
findings.user_impact: Supported operational inference: a recruiter interrupted by a call can interpret the definite failure as permission to recreate the person manually, or distrust the later existing-person match. This adds reconciliation work despite the underlying protected retry.
findings.recommendation: Must fix before exposure: for an uncertain transport/readback outcome, use one consistent message such as “We could not confirm the save. Check the original save to recover its result.” Reserve “not saved” for a definitive rejection or a failure before submission. Keep the original operation locked and remove first-save-only assurances while its result is unknown.
findings.verification: Repeat the existing after-commit response-loss/relaunch scenario. Before reconciliation every visible outcome label must remain uncertain, and the existing same-operation identity/receipt assertions must still pass. Also inspect a definitive pre-submission failure to ensure it can truthfully say nothing was saved.

findings.criterion: Interruption recovery: distinguish the fork from the conversation the recruiter already used
findings.observation: Direct observation: after a successful fork and native back gesture, the Sessions list shows two rows with the identical title and the identical “Agent conversation” context. Relative time and a generic “Refresh needed” status are the only visible differences. The model already stores originSessionID, but the row does not communicate that origin.
findings.evidence: /tmp/get5-product-review-v1/evidence/screenshots/12-native-back-original-and-fork-r7.png, both visible Session rows; /tmp/get5-product-review-v1/source/apps/ios/Sources/Features/RelationshipArchiveModels.swift:2655-2663 copies original.title and stores originSessionID; /tmp/get5-product-review-v1/source/apps/ios/Sources/Features/RelationshipArchiveView.swift:3579-3604 and :3644-3672 render title/context/accessibility label; /tmp/get5-product-review-v1/evidence/get5-ios-ui-final-r7.log:676 records the fork/native-back scenario passing.
findings.user_impact: Supported operational inference: after switching between several searches or returning later, the recruiter must open conversations or remember their timestamps to find the intended branch. “Refresh needed” describes source state and is not a stable branch identifier.
findings.recommendation: Add a quiet, persistent fork label derived from the existing origin relationship to the Session row and its accessibility label, for example “Fork of …”. Preserve the original title and content. This is a small retrieval improvement; a branch-management feature is unnecessary.
findings.verification: Fork a Session, add a different follow-up in each branch, restart and return to the list. The original and fork must be distinguishable without opening either row, including when both answers need refresh. Confirm both still open their respective message histories.

Must test with recruiters / value hypothesis: no observed comparison against copying a note or adding the contact manually establishes lower total effort, fewer missed commitments, or reduced correction burden. Use a small moderated task with seeded wrong-person/purpose errors and an interruption; measure source checking, corrections, duplicate entry, time to verified result and return-to-task accuracy. Do not turn this hypothesis into a field-usefulness claim.

The canonical provider trial proves that prior dialogue is supplied and “option two” is continued. Its generic request produces an applicant-to-recruiter email (/tmp/get5-product-review-v1/evidence/conversation-provider-proof.json:280-300), so it does not establish usefulness for a recruiter-owned candidate follow-up. That request is ambiguous; this review does not classify the result as a confirmed routing defect. The frozen screenshot UI case did not complete in either r6 or r7 (/tmp/get5-product-review-v1/evidence/get5-ios-ui-final-r6.log:759-761 and get5-ios-ui-final-r7.log:389-391). The backend 121-test result is stated in BRIEF.md without its own executable log in this manifest; this review does not upgrade that statement to directly inspected runtime proof.

The fallback when those images can no longer be reselected is untested. Establish how the recruiter resumes useful work while retaining an honest unresolved operation; the evidence does not justify removing the protected recovery gate.

Provider evidence is a bounded earlier recorded trial: several provider-proof source_sha256 values differ from the final manifest (/tmp/get5-product-review-v1/evidence/conversation-provider-proof.json:20-23). Final screenshot GLM trials, local TestFlight rebuild, deployed-source parity and physical-device VoiceOver are outside this packet and are not claimed complete.

findings.observation: Confirmed visible defect. In the English light contact-save response-loss state, the card says both “Previous outcome is unknown” and “The contact was not saved. Your proposal is still here.” The frozen catch branch supplies the latter fallback after a request whose outcome is already protected as pending. This is a false failure assertion, not evidence of duplicate writes or premature success.

missing_evidence: Evidence scope: reviewed all 14 frozen screenshots, relevant frozen iOS implementation/tests and supplied executable logs. The screenshot-to-source-detail-to-canonical-follow-up path remains unproven in this frozen native run. reviews.lens: evidence integrity, privacy, and safe action

findings.criterion: User authorization: deletion effect must match its preview
findings.observation: Confirmed in frozen code and supported by the executed store test: the deletion dialog promises deletion 'from this device' and says saved drafts remain unchanged, but its handler creates a synchronized deletion tombstone and removes this Session's contact proposal. Synchronization deletes the canonical Session; the database also retires screenshot tasks that no other live Session references. The preview understates both the device scope and the draft/processing effect. No native deletion-dialog capture was supplied.
findings.evidence: /tmp/get5-product-review-v1/source/apps/ios/Sources/Features/RelationshipArchiveView.swift:3221-3230 (preview), :704-706 (delete plus sync); source/apps/ios/Sources/Features/RelationshipArchiveModels.swift:1551-1553 (tombstone and proposal removal), :2859-2864 (canonical delete), :2759-2764 (remote tombstone application); source/apps/backend/src/database/054_agent_session_identifier_canonicalization.sql:82-101 (unreferenced screenshot retirement); source/apps/ios/Tests/AgentSessionContinuityTests.swift:293-310; evidence/get5-ios-unit-r8.log:80-81 records that test passing. All source/evidence shorthand paths are relative to /tmp/get5-product-review-v1.
findings.user_impact: A recruiter agreeing to remove a local copy can lose the conversation on another device, an unsaved contact draft, and unfiled screenshot processing context. This crosses the human-decision-to-deletion link with an inaccurately described effect.
findings.recommendation: Make canonical-mode deletion explicitly describe removal of the synced Session across devices, its unsaved Session drafts and unreferenced screenshot tasks. Preserve the accurate separate statement that filed People and workspace evidence follow their own lifecycle. Keep device-only wording only for a truly device-only preview store.
findings.verification: Capture the canonical deletion confirmation in English and Chinese, cancel once and confirm once, then verify two same-owner stores receive the tombstone; the affected proposal and unreferenced screenshot task are removed, while a referenced fork and separately filed source survive according to the displayed scope. Check the preview-mode wording separately.

findings.criterion: Privacy lifecycle: ordinary text replies need Session-linked retention and replay guards
findings.observation: Supported code risk, not a newly executed database result: a text-only Session reply receives no screenshot dependency record. On retry, createUnscopedChatTask returns the stored response before reading Session existence, owner scope or expiry. Its availability check returns true when there is no retracted task and no screenshot dependency. Session expiry/deletion clears agent_sessions.payload, while migration 055's response-body redaction requires a screenshot dependency. Consequently the inspected path retains and can replay a private text-derived answer after the Session is deleted or expires. The same early replay pattern exists in scoped Chat.
findings.evidence: /tmp/get5-product-review-v1/source/apps/backend/src/modules/unscopedChat.ts:224-243 (early replay), :286-287 (dependency record then full response persistence); source/apps/backend/src/modules/agentSessionSources.ts:139-147 (no dependencies means no record); source/apps/backend/src/database/055_agent_session_chat_sources.sql:38-59 (vacuous availability and screenshot-only body redaction); source/apps/backend/src/modules/agentSessions.ts:142-163 (expiry sweep), :654-655 and :708-722 (deleted Session payload); source/apps/backend/src/modules/chat.ts:800-818 (scoped replay). Required unchanged import /Users/cubxxw/data/talent-signal/apps/backend/src/lib/idempotency.ts:96-118 returns/persists response_body; it matches baseline d363ac04 and SHA-256 1a4d4aef5405658493e5a38200f40f9f56e75e9bc0696d71fd12acfdadc3b434. Frozen source/docs/architecture.md:175 states the thirty-day Session boundary. Existing source/apps/backend/src/modules/agentSessions.integration.test.ts:395-464 only proves Session payload/tombstone expiry, not this text-only reply store.
findings.user_impact: Sensitive details repeated by the assistant can remain in a replay store after the conversation's lifecycle ends. The source-to-derived-store deletion boundary is incomplete even when the native transcript correctly disappears.
findings.recommendation: Record the owning Session for every Session-backed Chat result, including text-only replies. Gate replay on the current same-owner Session lifecycle and physically redact the appropriate response bodies on deletion/expiry while retaining content-free operation identity. Define separately retained canonical task data explicitly rather than silently relying on it.
findings.verification: Add a normal PostgreSQL integration case that creates a synthetic text-only Session and answer, deletes the Session, retries the original operation, and expects unavailable/410 with the private answer absent from response_body. Repeat with the original thirty-day clock expired and with scoped Chat; a still-live same-owner Session must continue replaying its original result. The root owner should run this verification; this reviewer ran no network or database probe.

findings.criterion: External write integrity: distinguish unknown outcome from confirmed non-write
findings.observation: Confirmed visual defect: the response-loss screen simultaneously says 'Previous outcome is unknown' and 'The contact was not saved.' The fallback catch message asserts a negative result without knowing whether the server committed. The protected retry still uses the original operation, and the supplied later capture shows its canonical created-contact receipt.
findings.evidence: /tmp/get5-product-review-v1/evidence/screenshots/07-contact-response-lost-r6.png (both conflicting statements visibly present); evidence/screenshots/08-contact-same-operation-restored-r6.png (Contact created and canonical source receipt); source/apps/ios/Sources/Features/RelationshipAskView.swift:5049-5053 (fallback), :5670-5683 (unknown-result boundary); evidence/get5-ios-ui-final-r6.log:552 records testCanonicalContactResponseLossRelaunchRetriesSameOperation passing.

findings.verification: Repeat the supplied response-loss/relaunch case and inspect the full card, including its footer. It must contain no definitive 'not saved' or 'nothing changed' assertion before readback; retry must return the same canonical resource and operation receipt.

findings.criterion: Uncertainty: mixed evidence answers must retain the screenshot interpretation boundary
findings.observation: Supported presentation risk: markSessionContextAnswer enforces an unconfirmed screenshot title and proposed status only when an answer has no citations. A response combining unconfirmed screenshot context with one allowed reviewed citation bypasses that marker and remains informational. The provider instructions require attribution, but citation validation checks membership and count, not which claims came from the unconfirmed screenshot. This is not evidence of a particular provider producing a false confirmed claim or of a confirmed-state write.
findings.evidence: /tmp/get5-product-review-v1/source/apps/backend/src/modules/agentSessionSources.ts:6-20; source/apps/backend/src/modules/chat.ts:108-121 and :992-1004; source/apps/backend/src/modules/chatAnswerProvider.ts:367-396 and :485-486. source/apps/backend/src/modules/agentSessions.integration.test.ts:1637-1700 proves the citation-free case; source/apps/backend/src/modules/chatAnswerProvider.test.ts:644-651 proves internally admitted citation-free dialogue, not mixed-source attribution.
findings.user_impact: A recruiter can read a mixed answer as wholly grounded in the displayed reviewed citations, obscuring which part is an earlier screenshot interpretation. The interpretation-to-visible-answer boundary depends on generated wording in this case.
findings.recommendation: Keep an explicit unconfirmed-context indicator whenever screenshot dependencies contributed, including answers with reviewed citations; alternatively separate reviewed claims from screenshot interpretation in typed response blocks. Preserve current reviewed citation IDs and source withdrawal behavior.
findings.verification: Use one reviewed fact and one unresolved screenshot interpretation in a seeded provider result with a valid citation. Verify the visible response still identifies the screenshot portion as unconfirmed and that deleting either relevant source invalidates the corresponding answer as intended. Follow with a bounded actual-provider trial; do not treat a single trial as reliability measurement.

top_findings.criterion: User authorization: deletion effect must match its preview
top_findings.reason: Confirmed in frozen code and supported by the executed store test: the deletion dialog promises deletion 'from this device' and says saved drafts remain unchanged, but its handler creates a synchronized deletion tombstone and removes this Session's contact proposal. Synchronization deletes the canonical Session; the database also retires screenshot tasks that no other live Session references. The preview understates both the device scope and the draft/processing effect. No native deletion-dialog capture was supplied.
top_findings.next_step: Make canonical-mode deletion explicitly describe removal of the synced Session across devices, its unsaved Session drafts and unreferenced screenshot tasks. Preserve the accurate separate statement that filed People and workspace evidence follow their own lifecycle. Keep device-only wording only for a truly device-only preview store.
top_findings.verification: Capture the canonical deletion confirmation in English and Chinese, cancel once and confirm once, then verify two same-owner stores receive the tombstone; the affected proposal and unreferenced screenshot task are removed, while a referenced fork and separately filed source survive according to the displayed scope. Check the preview-mode wording separately.

top_findings.criterion: Privacy lifecycle: ordinary text replies need Session-linked retention and replay guards
top_findings.reason: Supported code risk, not a newly executed database result: a text-only Session reply receives no screenshot dependency record. On retry, createUnscopedChatTask returns the stored response before reading Session existence, owner scope or expiry. Its availability check returns true when there is no retracted task and no screenshot dependency. Session expiry/deletion clears agent_sessions.payload, while migration 055's response-body redaction requires a screenshot dependency. Consequently the inspected path retains and can replay a private text-derived answer after the Session is deleted or expires. The same early replay pattern exists in scoped Chat.
top_findings.next_step: Record the owning Session for every Session-backed Chat result, including text-only replies. Gate replay on the current same-owner Session lifecycle and physically redact the appropriate response bodies on deletion/expiry while retaining content-free operation identity. Define separately retained canonical task data explicitly rather than silently relying on it.
top_findings.verification: Add a normal PostgreSQL integration case that creates a synthetic text-only Session and answer, deletes the Session, retries the original operation, and expects unavailable/410 with the private answer absent from response_body. Repeat with the original thirty-day clock expired and with scoped Chat; a still-live same-owner Session must continue replaying its original result. The root owner should run this verification; this reviewer ran no network or database probe.

top_findings.criterion: Feedback/recovery (2/4): distinguish an unknown save outcome from a confirmed failure
top_findings.reason: Confirmed visible defect. In the English light contact-save response-loss state, the card says both “Previous outcome is unknown” and “The contact was not saved. Your proposal is still here.” The frozen catch branch supplies the latter fallback after a request whose outcome is already protected as pending. This is a false failure assertion, not evidence of duplicate writes or premature success.
top_findings.next_step: When the protected write remains pending, use one consistent message: “The save result is not confirmed. Check the original save.” Reserve “not saved” for a verified pre-write failure or definitive rejection. Keep the existing operation identity, locked fields and safe retry.
top_findings.verification: Repeat the existing response-loss/relaunch case. Before reconciliation, capture and assert that no visible or accessibility error says the contact was not saved; the screen consistently says the result is unknown. After retry, verify the original operation receipt and existing single destination identity. Also test a confirmed pre-write failure retains its accurate failure wording.
